clue.text: Make utterly clear but incomplete description of a lorry

indicators.note: incomplete tells us the descriptive word is cut short, losing its final letter

parts.note: an articulated lorry is one with a separate cab and trailer, so the describing word is articulated

explanation.surface: Someone praised for spelling things out plainly, yet whose account of a truck falls short.
explanation.walkthrough: 'incomplete' drops the final D from ARTICULATED. An articulated lorry is a British term for a tractor-trailer truck.
explanation.definitionFit: To articulate is to express or pronounce something distinctly, making it fully plain.

clue.text: Units currently supplied by a chemist

parts.note: MPS stands for Member of the Pharmaceutical Society, a qualified pharmacist

explanation.surface: Items in stock at the local pharmacy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'currently' is the pun: these units measure electric current. MPS is a British pharmacist's qualification.
explanation.definitionFit: The ampere is the standard unit of electric current.

clue.text: Swarm to encounter coming up

indicators.note: coming up, in a down clue, means the word is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: to encounter is to meet

explanation.surface: Bees massing to confront something approaching.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry 'coming up' reads MEET upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: To teem is to be full of moving creatures, crowding like a swarm.

clue.text: Forcing prisoners to have education

parts.note: cons is slang for convicts
training is instruction or schooling

explanation.surface: Making inmates go to classes against their will.
explanation.definitionFit: Constraining someone means compelling them by pressure.

clue.text: Beam embedded in wall — a serious matter

indicators.note: embedded in means the letters are set within the following words

explanation.surface: A structural timber set into a wall is a grave problem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'embedded in' points to letters running across 'wall — a serious'; 'matter' is padding.
explanation.definitionFit: A laser produces a narrow, intense beam of light.

clue.text: Joining the mainstream, one is bound to pay

explanation.surface: A person obliged to pay their way to get into the mainstream.
explanation.walkthrough: The word is both a stream feeding a river and, historically, a state obliged to pay tribute.
explanation.definitionFit: A side stream flows into a larger river; a vassal state owed tribute money to its overlord.

clue.text: Moulding for this pottery

parts.note: the clay is moulded into a celebrated Chinese porcelain named after a dynasty

explanation.surface: A craftsman's note on how a certain kind of pottery is shaped.
explanation.walkthrough: The pottery meant is the famous porcelain of a Chinese imperial dynasty (1368-1644); the clue simply describes shaping it.
explanation.definitionFit: A dynasty of China gave its name to the fine blue-and-white porcelain made in its reign.

clue.text: He urges us this month to go on a trip to Riga

parts.note: inst., short for instant, means this month in old business letters

indicators.note: going on a trip suggests the letters wander into a new order

explanation.surface: A man pressing us to fly to Riga this month.
explanation.walkthrough: INST (old commercial shorthand for 'this month') is followed by IGATOR, the letters of TO RIGA rearranged by 'go on a trip'.
explanation.definitionFit: An instigator is one who incites or provokes others to act.

clue.text: But no go-ahead to builders in these areas

definitions.text: But no go-ahead to builders in these areas

parts.words: But no go-ahead to builders in these areas
parts.note: planners give no green light for building here, despite the colour of the zone

explanation.surface: Builders are refused permission in certain zones.
explanation.walkthrough: The play is on 'green' meaning go-ahead: in these protected belts of countryside round British towns, building is not allowed.
explanation.definitionFit: These are protected rings of open land around cities where development is restricted.

clue.text: Synthetic substance including one variety that's redundant

indicators.note: including means the substance takes the other piece inside it

parts.note: plastic is a man-made, synthetic material

indicators.note: a variety of the word one is a different arrangement of its letters

explanation.surface: A man-made material containing one superfluous type, which turns out to be unnecessary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'redundant' here means superfluous in wording, not out of a job; 'variety' gives EON.
explanation.definitionFit: Pleonasm is the use of superfluous words, so a pleonastic phrase is wordy and needless.

clue.text: I shall shortly be heard in the Ely neighbourhood

indicators.note: be heard means we want a word that is spoken the same as the short form

parts.note: the contraction of I shall is I'll

explanation.surface: Someone promising they will soon be listened to in a Cambridgeshire cathedral city.
explanation.walkthrough: I'LL, the short form of 'I shall', is spoken just like the answer. Ely is a cathedral city in Cambridgeshire, England, and its area is historically called the Isle of Ely.
explanation.definitionFit: Ely stood on raised ground amid the fens, and its surrounding district was named as an island.

clue.text: Is unable to to reason with UK perhaps — so quarrelsome

parts.note: can't means is unable to

indicators.note: perhaps suggests the letters of reason and UK may be arranged differently

explanation.surface: Someone who cannot reason with Britain becomes argumentative.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' rearranges REASON and UK to ANKEROUS; the doubled 'to' is as printed and the spare one is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Cantankerous describes a bad-tempered, argumentative person.

clue.text: Position in which tuner is worried by sign of cold

indicators.note: in which means the position word holds the next piece within it

parts.note: a station is a post or position

indicators.note: worried suggests the word tuner is shaken up into a new order

explanation.surface: A piano tuner fretting over where he stands, shown up by a cold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sign of cold' is the definition, a sneeze; 'is worried' gives ERNUT, set inside by 'in which'.
explanation.definitionFit: Sternutation is the formal medical word for sneezing, the classic symptom of a head cold.

clue.text: I assume half-bottle maybe suffices such a one

indicators.note: maybe suggests the letters are arranged in another way
half of a six-letter word is its first three letters

explanation.surface: A drinker supposing a half-bottle is enough.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half-' takes BOT from 'bottle'; 'maybe' rearranges I ASSUME plus BOT.
explanation.definitionFit: A temperate person, sparing in drink, would be content with half a bottle.

clue.text: Smartened bird bound to swallow lots of wine

parts.note: a tit is a small bird

indicators.note: to swallow means the tied word takes the wine container inside

parts.note: bound means tied
a vat holds a large quantity of wine

explanation.surface: A bird, tied up, gulping a great deal of wine, looks spruced up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Smartened' carries the old spelling with double T; 'to swallow' signals the container.
explanation.definitionFit: To tittivate is to make small improvements to one's appearance.

clue.text: Yacht follows rule set down by Thomson

definitions.text: follows rule set down by Thomson

explanation.surface: A yacht trailing a regulation laid down by a man called Thomson.
explanation.walkthrough: James Thomson wrote the words of the British patriotic song 'Rule, Britannia!', so the name follows 'Rule' in its title. Britannia was also the British royal yacht.
explanation.definitionFit: The royal yacht bore the name of Britain's personification, which also comes after the word rule in Thomson's song title.

clue.text: Making egg-cups is strictly for the birds

definitions.text: Making egg-cups is strictly for the birds

parts.words: Making egg-cups is strictly for the birds
parts.note: the egg-cups are nests, which only birds construct

explanation.surface: Turning out egg-cups is a pointless pastime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strictly for the birds' usually means worthless; here it is literal, and the egg-cups are nests.
explanation.definitionFit: To nidify is to build a nest, the act birds perform to hold their eggs.

clue.text: Exchange beginning of text with read-out

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its opening letter
out suggests the letters of read are put out of order

explanation.surface: Swapping the start of a document for a version read aloud.
explanation.walkthrough: Take T from 'text', then 'out' rearranges READ to RADE.
explanation.definitionFit: Trade is buying and selling, the exchange of goods for money or other goods.

clue.text: Mythical Greek figure — it's in bronze

indicators.note: in means the first word goes inside the colour word

parts.note: bronze is a brownish colour, a tan
it's gives it, with is as a link

explanation.surface: A statue of a figure from Greek myth, cast in bronze.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of "it's" serves only as a link (it is in); 'in' signals the container.
explanation.definitionFit: The Titans were the race of giant gods who ruled before the Olympians in Greek mythology.

clue.text: Addict's treatment. Doctor applying female principle to painful illness

parts.note: yin is the feminine, passive principle in Chinese philosophy
gout is a painful inflammation of the joints

explanation.surface: A doctor treating an addict tries a feminine approach on a painful complaint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'applying ... to' just joins the pieces side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: Detoxification of an alcoholic or drug user is colloquially called this, as the body is rid of the substance.

clue.text: Having writ, shifty informer moves on

definitions.text: Having writ, shifty informer moves on

parts.note: shifty here means moving about, not settled
a finger is slang for an informer, one who fingers others to the police

explanation.surface: A treacherous informer, having written his statement, makes himself scarce.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue echoes FitzGerald's Rubaiyat: 'The Moving Finger writes; and, having writ, Moves on'.
explanation.definitionFit: In the famous quatrain, the finger writes our fate and, having written, passes on irrevocably.

clue.text: Name could be Eric, to be more precise

indicators.note: could be suggests the name Eric may be rearranged

explanation.surface: Being called Eric might make a person more exact.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could be' gives ICER; 'nice' keeps its older meaning of exact, so 'more precise' fits.
explanation.definitionFit: Nice in its older sense means fine or exact, as in a nice distinction.

clue.text: The spirit of Greece

parts.note: spirit means a strong drink, the national aniseed liquor rather than the country's soul

explanation.surface: The essential character of Greece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spirit' reads as national character but means an alcoholic drink.
explanation.definitionFit: This aniseed-flavoured liquor is Greece's national drink.

clue.text: Written texts hold key to confusion

indicators.note: hold means the texts surround the musical key

parts.note: MSS is the abbreviation for manuscripts
E is a musical key

explanation.surface: Written documents hold the clue to the muddle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hold' puts E inside MSS.
explanation.definitionFit: A mess is a state of disorder or muddle.

clue.text: As to ordering crop, ring auxiliary service

parts.note: a ring is round, the shape of the letter O
the ATS was the Auxiliary Territorial Service, the British women's army branch in WWII

explanation.surface: A farmer sorting out a crop and phoning the support services.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue gives two routes: 'As to ordering' is also a rearrangement of AS TO into OATS. The ATS was the women's branch of the British Army in the Second World War.
explanation.definitionFit: Oats are a cereal grain grown as a field crop.

clue.text: Record, nothing in the new rules it would be giveaway

parts.note: a disc is a gramophone record

indicators.note: in places the zero letter within the reshaped rules
new suggests the word rules is given a fresh arrangement

parts.note: nothing is zero, the letter O

explanation.surface: A new rulebook for records that would let a secret slip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' gives LSURE, and 'in' sets the zero inside it; the phrase 'it would be a' is linking padding.
explanation.definitionFit: A disclosure is a revealing of something hidden, the act that gives away a secret.

clue.text: Splash from this fountain

parts.note: a splash is a small dash of fizzy water added to a drink, as dispensed from a fountain at a drinks counter

explanation.surface: A spurt of water from an ornamental fountain.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'splash' is a dash of fizzy mixer in whisky; an American drugstore counter that serves fizzy drinks has the same kind of fountain.
explanation.definitionFit: Fizzy water comes from a siphon or fountain, and a splash of it tops up a spirit.

clue.text: They're first to adopt the best form of defence

definitions.text: They're first to adopt the best form of defence

parts.words: They're first to adopt the best form of defence
parts.note: the saying goes that attack is the best form of defence, so those who strike first are meant

explanation.surface: A tactical note on who takes up the strongest defensive posture first.
explanation.walkthrough: The proverb 'attack is the best form of defence' turns 'defence' into its opposite.
explanation.definitionFit: Those who start hostilities are the ones who launch the first attack.
